newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS - Hochtief sees profits down, orders strong.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Hochtief sees profits down, orders strong.

text.p: Hochtief AG, Germany's second largest construction group, said on Friday it expected full-year profits not quite to reach those in 1995 despite a strong gain in output for the year so far.
"As a whole we must assume that we shall not quite reach the net result shown in the previous year," the company said in a report by the management board to employees.
The company blamed weakness in the German building sector and charges associated with an internal restructuring for the expected profit fall.

Hochtief had previously given no precise forecast for the 1996 year except to say that it was hopeful of profit "continuity" in relation to the net profit of 137 million marks ($89.37 million) it made in 1995.
The report said that it was clear that continued strength in its international business would not fully offset an expected fall in its domestic profits.
But despite the profit warning, Hochtief saw its shares rise over five percent to 62 marks by the end of bourse trade in a move which baffled many construction analysts.
Some said that, given the overall gloom surrounding the German construction sector, there was a degree of relief that Hochtief was not signalling a greater decline in profits.
"But there is really no surprise. I think the share gains are a bit overdone," said on Frankfurt-based analyst.

The profit warning was followed later by publication of figures showing an 11.1 percent rise in nine-month building output to 8.82 billion marks, helped by a 28.5 percent gain in international output to 3.52 billion marks.
Incoming orders were 44.3 percent above the previous-year level at 11.8 billion marks, again helped by a large gain in international activity, where orders rose 94 percent to six billion marks.
But analysts noted that international orders had been boosted by a 2.38 billion mark one-off order for construction work on the Athens airport.

Separately, a Hochtief spokeswoman confirmed a newspaper report that the company was interested in pursuing "cooperation" possibilities with former takeover target Holzmann, in which it has a 20 percent stake.

Hochtief is currently seeking to overturn a German cartel office ruling preventing it from increasing its stake in Holzmann on the grounds that the two together would control too large a chunk of the German construction market.
"But it looks that whatever the outcome of the legal proceedings, Hochtief is determined that it should cooperate one way or the other with Holzmann," one analyst said.
